Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of South Africa who huddle-up before taking their places on the field. It will be the duo of Tanzid Hasan and skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto who will open the innings for Bangladesh. Marco Jansen will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Overall, Bangladesh will be mighty pleased with that bowling display as their pacers rose to the occasion and did some serious damage to the opposition. Tanzim Hasan Sakib bowled three overs upfront and got a wicket each in those overs and Taskin Ahmed too picked up one wicket. Surprisingly, their frontline spinners were off colour and Shakib Al Hasan bowled just the one over with Rishad Hossain going for plenty of runs. It was Mahmudullah who showed the best control of spin bowling. However, Rishad came back brilliantly and bowled a brave 19th over to David Miller and even got him out. Bangladesh closed off the innings brilliantly and now the onus will be on the batters to get 114 runs. It won't be straightforward and South Africa will come hard at them. Join us soon as the exciting run chase is coming up next.

The star with the ball for Bangladesh, Tanzim Hasan Sakib is down for a chat. He says they stick to the basic and the talk was just to bowl in the right areas. Mentions Quinton de Kock's wicket was his favourite as he hit him for couple of biggies before that. Reckons Taskin Ahmed got the wicket of Heinrich Klaasen at the perfect time. Ends by appreciating the support from the crowd.

Opting to bat first on a used pitch, the intent was made clear as Quinton de Kock decided to smash anything in his zone but as in the past couple of games, the opening stand faltered and Reeza Hendricks fell for a golden duck. Then came the collapse and all of a sudden, the Proteas were 23/4 inside the Powerplay. It was then a crucial stand between Heinrich Klaasen and their match winner from last time, David Miller worth 79 runs that got them in a good position at the backend but they simply couldn't kick on. Neither Klaasen nor Miller could stay on till the end and they might have missed out on 15-20 runs in the end.

A back and forth sort of a contest but at the halfway mark, Bangladesh will feel they pulled things back brilliantly at the death and have given themselves a wonderful platform. South Africa on the other hand will feel that they have runs on the board and will back their pacers. But have they done enough to salvage what could have been a disaster of a batting performance? Only time will tell.

Two runs to end the over. Just four runs off the final over! Serves it full and on middle, Marco Jansen eases it to long on, the batters push hard for two runs and gets it. South Africa end with 113 runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for action. First, we will have the national anthems. It will be of Bangladesh's first followed by of South Africa. Done with the formalities, we are all in readiness for the action now. Najmul Hossain Shanto is giving a last minute pep-talk to his team. Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks stride out to open for the Proteas. Tanzim Hasan Sakib to bowl first. A slip in place. Let's go...

Bangladesh skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto says that they would have bowled first anyway, so, they are happy. Informs that Jaker Ali has come in for Soumya Sarkar. Adds that wherever they play, the support is immense and they are happy with it. Mentions that he is happy with the boys after the previous win and believes they will do good here as well. Adds that they finally have a leg-spinner who has been consistent and hopes that they play some good cricket today.

Aiden Markram, the captain of South Africa says they will bat first as it is a used wicket. Feels the pitch could get slower as the game progresses and that could help their pacers. Reckons they back themselves to put on a good total. The trend is shifting to bat first and hopefully they do the job. Shares the batters need to find some forms, including himself, they just need a couple of good knocks to get back in form.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (WK), Tanzid Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Towhid Hridoy, Shakib Al Hasan, Mahmudullah, Jaker Ali (In for Soumya Sarkar), Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Mustafizur Rahman.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Reeza Hendricks, Aiden Markram (C), Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller, Tristan Stubbs, Marco Jansen, Keshav Maharaj, Kagiso Rabada, Anrich Nortje, Ottneil Baartman.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of South Africa. They have decided to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - It is the third game we are playing on the same surface, once again it won't be easy for the batters. The back of the length delivery and hard-length delivery could help the bowlers as it would be hard for batters to hit the longer square boundaries.

South Africa on the other hand have played two and won two and a win here against Bangladesh will see them take pole position in Group D and would all but guarantee a passage to the next round. In both their games, the Proteas have bowled extremely well but we have also seen them falter with the bat. They will count themselves a bit lucky against Netherlands as David Miller and Tristan Stubbs pulled them out of trouble and the former even went on to score a match-winning half-century. We already know that this pitch will aid the bowlers, so, it will really come down to which side can have that mental fortitude with the bat. Can South Africa overome another stern challenge and get one foot into the Super Eights? Or will Bangladesh rise up and go level on points with them? We shall find out. Toss and teams in a bit.

Bangladesh have played one match so far and that was a very close encounter against Sri Lanka in Dallas. With a win under their belt, the players will be confident of notching up an upset against a Proteas side that didn't look like a tournament favorite in their last game against Netherlands. Bangladesh do have the bowling attack to trouble the best of teams but it is all about consistency and that batting lineup needs to back the bowlers if they are to get the win.

Hello and welcome back to the Nassau County Cricket Stadium in New York where less than 24 hours ago we witnessed an epic encounter between two eternal rivals, India and Pakistan. The venue has seen a game daily since the 7th of June and to kick off a new week in the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024, we have Bangladesh taking on South Africa in a Group D clash. Both teams are unbeaten so far and will look to battle it out for supremacy in this group and thankfully, it is a fairly sunny morning in New York.
... MATCH DAY ...

South Africa has kicked off this World Cup with two impressive wins, edging closer to a spot in the Super Eight. However, their victory over the Netherlands wasn't easy, with a gritty half-century from David Miller and a crucial contribution from Tristan Stubbs getting them across the line. Now, another tricky challenge awaits as they prepare to face Bangladesh. South Africa's bowling has been fantastic so far, with Anrich Nortje leading the pace attack and finding his rhythm. Ottneil Baartman has been brilliant, especially at the death, while Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen add strength to their formidable attack. Keshav Maharaj has done well as the lone spinner, and Stubbs can pitch in if needed. However, their batting needs to step up if they want to challenge the big guns. Quinton de Kock will be key at the top, while more is expected from Aiden Markram and Reeza Hendricks. Heinrich Klaasen has the potential to be lethal but needs to be more patient on tricky pitches. With a few tweaks, South Africa could become a force to reckon with in this tournament. Bangladesh, on the other hand, started their campaign with a thrilling win over their Asian rivals, Sri Lanka. Veteran Mahmudullah grabbed the two points with a quick cameo in a crunch situation. Litton Das provided a good start but needs to show more intent, while Towhid Hridoy was excellent, top-scoring in the last game. Soumya Sarkar, Tanzid Hasan, and Najmul Hossain Shanto need to take on more responsibility in the batting unit. Much will depend on Shakib Al Hasan, who can contribute in both departments, and with this being his last T20 World Cup, he'll be eager to perform well. Their bowling attack is solid, with Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, and Tanzim Hasan Sakib forming a strong pace battery, while Rishad Hossain complements Shakib in the spin department. Mahmudullah also provides a decent option. Their collective effort in the last game restricted Sri Lanka to under 130, and they’ll aim to pressure the Proteas' batters who have shown vulnerability. The stakes are high. Will South Africa make it three wins in a row, or will Bangladesh stop them in their tracks? We’ll find out soon in what promises to be another thrilling encounter! Word count: 362
